$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.format.wrap. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-GROUPIFY-GATE-REFOLD-OFF
arms.note: a comprehension item's re-tag widens a chain gate's flat side without re-folding its threshold, so the gate counts the body twice and breaks a chain that fits

arms.name: M-CUDDLE-FLATONLY
arms.note: restores the pre-S146 gate — only an item that CANNOT render flat cuddles, so a comprehension that renders flat and still overflows keeps its `[` on a line of its own

arms.name: M-CUDDLE-FALLBACK-INDENT
arms.find: final item: Null<Doc> = itemFlat < 0 ? items[0] : dropComprehensionBody(items[0]);
arms.replace: final item: Null<Doc> = itemFlat < 0 ? items[0] : cols + itemFlat <= lineWidth ? null : dropComprehensionBody(items[0]);
arms.note: restores the S146 threshold — a flat item that fits the line `shapeOnePerLine` would give it keeps its own bracket line, so a comprehension whose item fits one indent deeper but not after `[ ` is refused the cuddle (T674)

arms.name: M-CUDDLE-OFF
arms.note: the comprehension cuddled-open shape never fires, so `[ for (…)` goes back to its own bracket line

arms.name: M-ELSE-GATE
arms.note: restores the S76 veto S78 removed — a comprehension whose body is an if/else refuses to cuddle its `[` again

arms.name: M-FN-LAMBDA-BODY-DEFERRED
arms.note: no `function`-keyword lambda argument opens the BodyGroup re-tag gate, so its parked inline body measures 0 again and the callParameter / methodChain / ifBody cascades above it all read a line short by the whole body - the fixed point of any width the Pony site showed at 146 columns

arms.name: M-GROUPIFY-SHARED-OFF
arms.note: regrouping a comprehension's items copies every shared Doc node once per path to it, so the writer's Doc grows 2^depth

arms.name: M-BREAK-MULTI-ITEM-HOST-OFF
arms.find: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : open != '{';
arms.replace: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : false;
arms.note: a list of several items stops following a break nested in one of them, so a call around `bar(b, [for …])` stays glued while the literal breaks under it and the next write opens it one argument per line

arms.name: M-BREAK-OBJECT-LITERAL-HOST
arms.find: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : open != '{';
arms.replace: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : true;
arms.note: an object literal's field list is wrapped in alternatives too, which hides the literal's width decision from its Allman placement: a comprehension body carrying a comprehension in a field breaks glued and goes Allman one write late

arms.name: M-FORCED-NOWRAP-UNPROBED
arms.note: a list a source trailing separator forces into the break-mode cascade goes flat by a shadowing `noWrap` rule with no first-line probe, past the limit, where the unforced first write broke it

arms.name: M-REGION-OFFER-THROUGH-BODIES
arms.note: a list lays itself out for a region inside a comprehension body, whose own seam the next write re-decides

arms.name: M-CHAIN-REST-PIVOT-PLAIN
arms.note: the chain pivot decides on `col + flatWidth` alone, so a chain whose physical line runs two columns over (the `;` and the space after `=`) stays glued and breaks before a nested `==`

arms.name: M-CHAIN-REST-ADD-PIVOT-PLAIN
arms.note: the tagged `+` chain pivot ignores the rest of its line, so a declaration one column over the limit spills past it unbroken

arms.name: M-CHAIN-REST-FILL-GROUP-PLAIN
arms.note: the fill shape's own group re-decides flat on `col + flatWidth` inside the broken pivot, so a chain one column over breaks before a nested `==` instead of at `&&`

arms.name: M-CHAIN-REST-SHAPE-UNTHREADED
arms.find: return shape(r.mode, r.location, items, ops, cols, indentUnit, cuddleLast, restAware, list);
arms.replace: return shape(r.mode, r.location, items, ops, cols, indentUnit, cuddleLast, false, list);
arms.note: `restAware` never reaches the shapes, so the fill group stays plain and undoes the rest-aware pivot's break

arms.name: M-CHAIN-REGION-OFFER-OFF
arms.note: a chain is never offered for a break nested in a part, so the link after a call whose region breaks stays on its own line and the next write cuddles it

arms.name: M-CHAIN-CLOSE-UNRESOLVED
arms.note: the offer gate reads the committed part on the flat side of the conditional around the region, sees no closing line and offers nothing

arms.name: M-CHAIN-AFTERFIRST-COMMIT-UNREAD
arms.note: the offered layout of a chain whose head is not a call reads the committed part flat, so the offer lays the link out uncuddled as before

arms.name: M-CHAIN-ONEPERLINE-COMMIT-UNREAD
arms.note: the offered layout of a chain with a call head reads the committed part flat, so the offer lays the link out uncuddled as before

arms.name: M-THRESHOLD-ARG-UNNAMED
arms.note: an object-literal argument deciding its own threshold break is no longer named, so the argument list lays itself out from the flat literal and the next write, reading the broken literal back committed, packs the list differently

arms.name: M-CHAIN-OFFER-OFF
arms.note: a binary chain or ternary no longer re-lays itself out for an operand whose nested break commits, so a ternary hugs a call whose literal broke and the next write, reading that literal back with a hardline, breaks the ternary

arms.name: M-ELIDED-GAP-HARD
arms.note: every gap the source left without a separator is a forced line break again, so a parameter list that fits breaks after `#end`

arms.name: M-REGION-GLUED
arms.note: a region behind an elided separator glues onto the previous parameter's line, where `= false #if air, …` re-parses as a splice tail of the default value

arms.name: M-ELIDED-SEP-KEPT
arms.find: final elided: Bool = [for (k in from + 1...to) skipSepBefore(sepBeforeFlags, k)].contains(true);
arms.note: a fill run packs with one uniform separator, so a gap the source left comma-less gains a comma beside the one its region already wrote

arms.name: M-TRAIL-AFTER-REGION
arms.note: a region ending the list takes the trailing comma again, which compiles to `, ,` once its branch is off

arms.name: M-TRAIL-AFTER-SEMI
arms.note: a class-notation structure field takes the trailing comma after its own `;`

arms.name: M-TRAIL-CASCADE-UNGATED
arms.note: the wrap cascade appends the trailing comma whatever the last item ends on

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-INLINE-NONE
arms.find: if (inlineMultilineBranch) return IfFirstLineExceeds(opt.lineWidth, broken, shapeNoWrap(items, ops));
arms.note: the inline verdict is never read, so `ternaryMultilineBranch: inline` breaks the ternary like `break`

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-NO-WIDTH-GUARD
arms.note: `inline` glues the ternary whatever the width, so a first line past the limit overflows

arms.name: M-RULE-LOCATION-FALLS-TO-DEFAULT
arms.note: a matched rule that names no location takes the section's `defaultLocation` instead of `afterLast`, so the default overrides a rule that matched

arms.name: M-CHAIN-THRESHOLD-WRAPS-PIVOT
arms.find: emitCascadePivot(items, ops, opt, nestSuppress, condWrapForced, restAware, evalAt, shapeAt, shapeNoWrapAt, extraThresholds);
arms.replace: extraThresholds.length == 0 ? emitCascadePivot(items, ops, opt, nestSuppress, condWrapForced, restAware, evalAt, shapeAt, shapeNoWrapAt, []) : WrapBoundary(Group(IfBreak(thresholdTree(extraThresholds, [], true, evalAt, shapeAt), thresholdTree(extraThresholds, [], false, evalAt, shapeAt))));
arms.note: a cascade holding a lineLength rule wraps a plain Group around its exceeds pivot, which no longer counts the line's trailing columns nor carries the add-chain collapse marker

arms.name: M-CHAIN-THRESHOLD-UNIFORM-BLIND
arms.find: return reached != null && below != null && sameRule(reached, below) ? below : null;
arms.note: every threshold state is taken to answer as the one below it, so a lineLength rule the line reaches below the limit never fires

arms.name: M-CHAIN-THRESHOLD-REEVAL-UNTAGGED
arms.find: final brkSide: Doc = thresholdTree(thresholds, [], true, evalAt, brkShapeAt);
arms.replace: final brkSide: Doc = thresholdTree(thresholds, [], true, evalAt, thresholds.length == 0 ? brkShapeAt : shapeAt);
arms.note: a cascade holding a lineLength rule never tags its trailing-operator fill for the opBool re-eval, so a chain whose call operand overflows keeps its trailing operators

arms.name: M-CHAIN-HUG-LAST
arms.note: a chain whose only multi-line operand is the last one breaks before it instead of hugging it, so `a && xs.foreach(t -> {` moves the call to its own line

arms.name: M-RULE-MATCH-IGNORED
arms.note: a matched rule answers the section default, so neither its mode nor its operator side reaches the chain

arms.name: M-RULE-CONDITIONS-IGNORED
arms.note: every rule matches whatever its conditions say, so the first rule of a cascade answers for every list and chain

arms.name: M-HUG-ANY-FIRST-LINE
arms.note: the chain hugs its last operand whenever the glued first line fits, so a  line inside that operand glues the chain to it

arms.name: M-CHAIN-ABOVE-NEXT-UNBLOCKED
arms.note: under beforeLast the operand after a moved comment still counts as opening a line after an operator, so its comment moves too and the next pass reads it back elsewhere

arms.name: M-CHAIN-ABOVE-LED-IGNORED
arms.note: an operand already led by an own-line comment takes a moved comment above it too

arms.name: M-CONTCOLS-NO-ADDITIONAL
arms.note: the matched rule additionalIndent is never charged, so a wrapped list stays one unit deep whatever its cascade says

arms.name: M-CONTCOLS-DEFAULT-ONLY
arms.note: every break charges the cascade default indent, so a matched rule stating its own indent is overridden

arms.name: M-CONTCOLS-IGNORE-SUPPRESS
arms.note: a function signature over an empty body charges the additional indent like any other

arms.name: M-CONTCOLS-LEADING-BREAK-INDENT
arms.note: a leading-break line charges the additional indent, one unit deeper than its first line belongs

arms.name: M-HERITAGE-RULE-INDENT
arms.note: a matched heritage rule keeps the cascade default indent instead of its own

arms.name: M-ELEM-CHAIN-OFF
arms.note: every case pattern list takes the plain list layout again, so `|` stays inside its element and breaks one per line after the first overflow

arms.name: M-ELEM-CHAIN-LEADS-OFF
arms.note: a list with no alternative stays on the list layout under `beforeLast`, whose `,` always ends the line

arms.name: M-ELEM-CHAIN-GUARD-MEASURED
arms.note: the guard joins the last operand, so the chain breaks to make room for a condition that wraps on its own

arms.name: M-LIST-CHAIN-RESERVE-LOOSE
arms.note: a list chain packs one column further than the `,` list path, so an element ending past the budget stays on the line

arms.name: M-LIST-CHAIN-RESERVE-TIGHT
arms.note: a list chain packs one column short of the `,` list path, so an element ending on the budget breaks

arms.name: M-LIST-SEP-TIGHT-OFF
arms.find: final tightGaps: Bool = listSep != null && ops.contains(listSep);
arms.note: a leading `,` keeps the soft line's space in front of it while the line holds: `a , b`

arms.name: M-ELEM-CHAIN-INDENT-DROPPED
arms.note: a cascade naming an additional indent reaches the chain, whose answer carries mode and location only, so the indent stops answering

arms.name: M-ELEM-CHAIN-TAKES-IGNORE
arms.note: an `ignore` label holding `|` moves to the chain on the built-in rules, away from what that mode writes

arms.name: M-LIST-CHAIN-CLOSER-GLUED
arms.note: an opened label holding `|` glues its `:` to the last operand while a plain list puts it alone

arms.name: M-ELEM-CHAIN-HARDLINE-OPERAND
arms.note: an operand opening with a hardline joins the fill, whose flat gap leaves a space at the line end and takes a second rewrite

arms.name: M-CHAIN-LITERAL-NAMED
arms.note: a ternary lays itself out from the flat literal in its branch, so the first write takes the cascade's break where the next one, reading the broken literal, keeps the ternary on one line

arms.name: M-TERNARY-NAMES-FIT-PIVOT
arms.note: a ternary operand literal deciding its break by fit is not named, so a branch literal that breaks under the compiled defaults leaves the ternary broken on the first write and glued on the next

arms.name: M-CUDDLE-WRAPPED-HEAD
arms.note: a flat-capable item measures its cuddled head by the line it would naturally render, so a head too wide for `[ for (` cuddles anyway and wraps its own iterable call instead of falling back to the leading break

arms.name: M-FILL-TRAIL-SEP-UNGATED
arms.note: a fill-laid list that stays on one line gets the comma a trailingCommas add-knob asks for, which is meant for a broken list only

arms.name: M-FILL-TRAIL-SEP-DROPPED
arms.note: a fill-laid list broken over lines loses the comma a trailingCommas add-knob asks for

arms.name: M-FILL-FLAT-SOURCE-TRAIL-OFF
arms.note: a fill-laid list that stays on one line drops the trailing comma its source wrote under keep

arms.name: M-COLLECTION-ARG-FLAT-SOURCE-TRAIL-OFF
arms.note: a call holding a collection argument that stays on one line drops the trailing comma its source wrote under keep

arms.name: M-SOLE-ARG-ADD-COMMA
arms.note: a sole argument that shares the open delimiter's line gets the comma a trailingCommas add-knob asks for when its own content breaks or overflows

arms.name: M-GLUE-SOURCE-TRAIL-OFF
arms.note: a call glued around a multi-line collection argument drops the trailing comma its source wrote under keep

arms.name: M-BLOCK-LAMBDA-GLUE-SOURCE-TRAIL-OFF
arms.note: a leading-break call glued around a block lambda drops the trailing comma its source wrote under keep
